BiblicalUsage: Zuwd is the Aramaic word for acting proudly or presumptuously — Daniel uses it once, for Nebuchadnezzar, whose heart was lifted up and his mind hardened in pride until he was deposed from his throne. One word carries the whole fall: pride rose, and the king fell.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Nebuchadnezzar's fall is the warning in this word: a heart lifted up against God will be brought down.
